subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add a native Gateway multi-token principal model for Control UI/webchat token-mode users, and should it be unified with the scoped-token work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92367?
rationale: The request changes public auth config, credential matching, caller identity, authorization scopes, session isolation, and security docs, so automation should not choose the permanent trust model.

options.title: Design unified Gateway principals
options.body: Define a single security model covering per-user tokens, scoped service tokens, SecretRefs, rotation, docs, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to user labels first
options.body: Implement only token-to-user labels and session identity for Control UI/webchat now, accepting a likely later migration into broader scoped principals.

options.title: Keep external front layers
options.body: Decline native multi-token auth for now and document trusted-proxy or Pinchy-style front layers as the supported team-deployment path.

recommendation.title: Design unified Gateway principals
recommendation.body: Define a single security model covering per-user tokens, scoped service tokens, SecretRefs, rotation, docs, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: nickytonline introduced the current identity-bearing trusted-proxy auth path, which is the closest existing Gateway user-identity boundary.
